item.title: Grace Has Authority
item.description:
Yesterday I wrote about grace as receiving what we do not deserve. But there is another part of grace that I think is easy to miss: grace is only as meaningful as the authority of the person giving it.

At the end of my university years I had accumulated a lot of debt. Some of it was simply the cost of living and studying; some of it, if I am honest, was not always spent particularly wisely. Either way, it was thousands and thousands of pounds, and it was mine. I had incurred it and there was no reasonable argument that somebody else should carry it for me.

item.title: Grace: What We Don't Deserve
item.description:
When we talk about grace, it can become one of those Christian words that we understand without always feeling the full weight of it. We know the definition: unmerited favour. Something given to us that we have not earned and do not deserve.

Perhaps the easiest way to understand grace is to remember what it feels like to receive an unexpected gift, particularly when you were expecting something very different.
